relative-and-absolute-paths.label: Relative and Absolute Paths
relative-and-absolute-paths.summary: Understand how URLs and local paths point to resources.

try_relative_and_absolute_paths_sketch0.title: Try it yourself: Use a same-folder path
try_relative_and_absolute_paths_sketch0.prompt: Now apply what you just learned in this task. The Explorer shows `index.html` and `about.html` side by side. In `index.html`, connect `About me` to the neighboring page using a relative path. Produce the result for use a same-folder path so it reinforces Relative and Absolute Paths.
try_relative_and_absolute_paths_sketch0.hint: No folder change is needed for this destination.

help.concept: A same-folder relative path can connect sibling HTML files without a full web address.
help.hint_1: The destination file is visible beside the current file in Explorer.
help.hint_2: Use only the neighboring page's filename as the destination.

paths-sc-1.title: Choose a same-folder path
paths-sc-1.prompt: Which href points to `about.html` in the same folder as the current page?
paths-sc-1.hint: A same-folder relative path can name the file directly.

help.concept: Relative paths are interpreted from the current document location.
help.hint_1: No folder change is needed for a file in the same directory.

paths-sc-2.title: Choose an absolute URL
paths-sc-2.prompt: Which destination is an absolute web URL?
paths-sc-2.hint: Look for a complete URL with a scheme and host.

help.concept: Absolute URLs include the full network destination.
help.hint_2: Relative paths do not need a scheme or hostname.

paths-mc-1.title: Recognize relative paths
paths-mc-1.prompt: Which values are relative paths? Choose all that apply.
paths-mc-1.hint: Relative paths depend on the current file location.

help.concept: Relative paths can name same-folder, child-folder, or parent-folder destinations.
help.hint_1: A full https URL is absolute.
help.hint_2: Look for values without a scheme and host.

paths-dr-1.title: Build a child-folder path
paths-dr-1.prompt: Arrange these pieces to form a relative path to `contact.html` inside the `pages` folder.
paths-dr-1.hint: Start with the folder, then the slash, then the file.

help.concept: A child-folder path names the folder before the file.

paths-fb-1.title: Complete a parent-folder path
paths-fb-1.prompt: Choose the prefix that moves from a child folder up to its parent before opening `index.html`.
paths-fb-1.hint: Use the path segment that means parent folder.

help.hint_1: The target file is outside the current folder.

paths-fb-2.title: Complete an external destination
paths-fb-2.prompt: Choose the value that makes this link point to the complete Example site profile URL.
paths-fb-2.hint: An external destination needs the complete absolute URL.

help.concept: Absolute web URLs include scheme and host.
help.hint_1: The destination is on example.com, not this site's folder tree.

relative-paths-start-from-current-locati.title: Relative paths start from the current file
relative-paths-start-from-current-locati.bodyMarkdown: A relative path tells the browser where a destination is **from the current HTML file**. ```html Tutoring schedule Campus events ``` Line by line: **First**, `schedule.html` tells the browser to look in the same folder as the current page. **Second**, `pages/events.html` tells the browser to enter the `pages` child folder before opening `events.html`. Relative paths are useful when related site files move together because the path is based on their folder relationship.

absolute-urls-name-complete-destinations.title: Absolute URLs name a complete destination
absolute-urls-name-complete-destinations.bodyMarkdown: An absolute URL includes the scheme and host, so the browser has the full destination. ```html Campus map ``` This line gives the browser a complete external destination: the scheme is `https`, the host is `example.org`, and `/campus-map` identifies the resource on that site. Unlike a relative path, the destination does not depend on the current HTML file's folder.

dot-dot-moves-up-one-folder.title: Use ../ to move up one folder
dot-dot-moves-up-one-folder.bodyMarkdown: `../` means “move to the parent folder.” If `profile.html` is inside `students/`, this link: ```html Site home ``` This line first moves from `students/` to its parent folder, then asks the browser to open `home.html` there. Read a relative path from left to right: move through the folder relationship first, then arrive at the target file.
